newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Toyota shares driven up by Japanese deal. [CORRECTED 16:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Toyota shares driven up by Japanese deal. [CORRECTED 16:10 GMT]

text.p: Shares in Toyota South Africa Ltd jumped 12 percent on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on Tuesday on news Japan's Toyota Motor Corp (TMC) had bought a stake in the South African motor manufacturer.
Analysts and dealers said the market had welcomed the deal as it would boost Toyota's SA's access to new technology and improve its export performance.

"The market has responded favourably as the company now has a better future... It will get new technology and also real support from Toyota Japan for its export drive," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
TMC announced on Tuesday it would buy a 27.8 percent stake in Toyota SA from Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd (Johnnic) for 446 million rand (corrects from 456 million rand).
By 1240 GMT shares in Toyota SA had climbed 430 cents to the day's peak of 35.80 rand, just short of this year's best level of 36 rand.

However, volumes traded remained small a fact which dealers said was due to players having expected the deal which has been speculated about since mid-July. Some 33,200 shares had changed hands in 29 deals.
Analysts said shares were likely to creep higher in the short term, closer to 40.30 rand level a share at which the deal was priced.
"On the basis of the deal, traders are putting a value of about 40 rand on Toyota's shares," a dealer said.
Announcing the deal earlier on Tuesday, TMC senior managing director, Shinji Sakai said the purchase was in response to President Nelson Mandela's request for investment from Japan.
